questions.text: What is the core idea behind LoRA (Low-Rank Adaptation)?
options: Replacing all weight matrices with smaller random matrices
Pruning unimportant neurons to reduce model size
Freezing original weights and learning low-rank update matrices that are added to them
Training only the embedding layer while keeping all other layers fixed
questions.explanation: LoRA freezes the original pre-trained weights and introduces trainable low-rank decomposition matrices (A and B) whose product is added to the original weight matrix. This dramatically reduces the number of trainable parameters while maintaining model quality.

questions.text: In LoRA, a weight update is represented as W + BA, where B has shape (d x r) and A has shape (r x k). What does the rank r control?
options: The number of attention heads in the model
The expressiveness and number of trainable parameters in the low-rank update
The batch size used during training
The number of layers that are frozen
questions.explanation: The rank r determines the dimensionality of the low-rank decomposition. A higher rank allows more expressive updates but increases the number of trainable parameters. Typical values range from 4 to 64 depending on the task complexity.

questions.text: Which of the following are benefits of using LoRA compared to full fine-tuning? Select all that apply
options: It always outperforms full fine-tuning on every task
Lower GPU memory requirements during training
Multiple LoRA adapters can be swapped without reloading the base model
questions.explanation: LoRA trains far fewer parameters (often <1% of the model), requires less GPU memory since optimizer states are only needed for the small adapter matrices, and allows hot-swapping adapters for different tasks on the same base model. It does not always outperform full fine-tuning.

questions.text: What distinguishes QLoRA from standard LoRA?
options: QLoRA uses a higher rank for better performance
QLoRA applies LoRA only to query projection matrices
QLoRA replaces the transformer architecture with a quantized variant
QLoRA quantizes the base model to 4-bit precision and trains LoRA adapters in higher precision on top
questions.explanation: QLoRA combines 4-bit NormalFloat quantization of the frozen base model with LoRA adapter training in BFloat16/Float16 precision. This enables fine-tuning of very large models on consumer GPUs while maintaining near-full-precision quality.

questions.text: If a weight matrix W has dimensions 4096 x 4096 and LoRA uses rank r=16, how many trainable parameters does the LoRA adapter add for that single matrix?
questions.explanation: LoRA adds matrices B (4096 x 16) and A (16 x 4096), totaling 4096 x 16 + 16 x 4096 = 65,536 + 65,536 = 131,072 parameters. Compare this to the original 4096 x 4096 = 16,777,216 parameters -- a 128x reduction.
